findings: Invoices seed data column mismatch — The INSERT statement lists 11 columns (MemberId through IsDeleted) but the SELECT provides only 10 values. Add `i.MemberId,` after the SELECT keyword to align the value count.

Schema fix ALTER statements lack IF NOT EXISTS guards — Several ALTER TABLE statements (making InvoiceId nullable, making MembershipId nullable, making DueDate nullable, making UpdatedAt nullable) execute unconditionally and would fail on re-run if the column is already nullable. Wrap each ALTER COLUMN in a check: `IF EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.columns WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID('TableName') AND name = 'ColumnName' AND is_nullable = 0) BEGIN ... END`.

Admin cancel bypasses controller auth but not service auth — The cancel endpoint lets admin/superadmin roles skip the ownership check in the controller, but then passes `membership.MemberId` to `_service.CancelAsync(id, membership.MemberId)`, which performs the same ownership check in the service layer. Either remove the requestingMemberId parameter from the service and repository methods (ownership check belongs in controller only), or change the controller to pass the admin's own MemberId and handle the authorization check consistently in one layer.

Schedule StartTime/EndTime conversion assumes combined datetime — The schema fix script converts `ScheduledDate + StartTime/EndTime (TIME)` to `StartTime/EndTime (DATETIME2)` by casting and adding. This only works if the existing Schedules table actually has ScheduledDate and TIME-type columns. If the table was already using DATETIME2 columns, the rename step would fail because StartTime already exists.
